owner_posts.post_text: Phone addiction has become one of the biggest parenting challenges today. Parents struggle with setting boundaries, managing constant conflicts, monitoring online safety and competing with the appeal of screens. Many also feel guilty because they use phones themselves. The goal is not to eliminate technology, but to teach children balance, responsibility and healthy digital habits.

Growing up, many of us were taught that parents are the safest people to talk to. But sometimes children don’t need advice, solutions, or life lessons — they just need to feel heard. When emotions are dismissed often enough, silence slowly starts feeling safer than honesty. And what looks like distance is sometimes just someone protecting parts of themselves that once felt misunderstood.

Sometimes I wonder how a person can be considered “too young” to fully understand consequences, yet old enough to commit something so horrific. It’s difficult to balance accountability with the belief that people can change.

We often underestimate how stressed corporate professionals can be. Long hours, constant deadlines, endless notifications, pressure to always perform, and the inability to truly switch off slowly take a toll. Just because someone is sitting in an office, dressed well, and functioning normally does not mean they are mentally okay. Think about it.
Yet another time with one of my favourites,

Working with Godrej has always been a fun-filled experience—each time they come up with something unique that has a psychological tinge to it. This time, we explored how safe spaces actually change our perceptions and perspectives. 

Hyderabad was fun.
Another city coming soon.

Children today are growing up inside powerful digital systems that shape attention, self-worth and emotional safety. Instead of reacting with outrage or blanket bans, the conversation must centre on protection. Thoughtful guardrails and digital literacy can help young people build resilience before stepping into a world designed to capture them.

I am often asked, “In a room full of testosterone, does your cortisol soar?”
Well, no but my dopamine certainly does. And toward the end, my serotonin spikes too. The only one periodically off the charts is insulin -  but yes, oxytocin will always be my favourite.

Many people ignore strange sensations in their legs until the pain becomes severe. But your body often gives warning signs much earlier.
If you experience tingling in legs, burning sensation in legs, or a constant pins and needles sensation, it could be a sign of nerve pain in leg caused by irritation or compression of nerves.
One of the most common reasons behind these symptoms is sciatica nerve pain, where the sciatic nerve gets irritated in the lower back or hip. This can lead to leg numbness causes, tingling in legs, and sometimes even leg weakness causes. Many people also experience a burning sensation in legs that travels down the thigh or calf.
In some cases, nerve compression symptoms can develop due to prolonged sitting, poor posture, disc irritation, or tight muscles. When the nerve is irritated, it can produce sensations like pins and needles sensation, tingling in legs, or sharp nerve pain in leg.
Another possible reason for these symptoms is peripheral neuropathy symptoms, where nerves become sensitive and start sending abnormal signals like burning sensation in legs, numbness, or weakness.
Sometimes people also notice leg swelling causes along with heaviness and discomfort, which may increase pressure around nerves and worsen sciatica symptoms or nerve compression symptoms.
The good news is that many of these problems can improve with proper physiotherapy for nerve pain.

At first glance, it looks like this person is simply strapped to a moving table... but what if I told you this machine is actually creating space inside the spine to help relieve back pain and sciatica?
What you're seeing is Spinal Decompression Therapy, a specialized non-surgical treatment commonly used for people suffering from chronic lower back pain, sciatica, bulging discs, herniated discs, and certain degenerative spinal conditions.
So how does it work?
The motorized table applies a gentle, controlled pulling force to the lumbar spine (lower back). This creates a process called **decompression**, where the vertebrae are slightly separated, reducing pressure on the spinal discs and nearby nerves.
Why is this important?
🦴 Reduces Disc Pressure
Spinal discs act as shock absorbers between your vertebrae. When a disc bulges or herniates, it can press on nearby nerves and cause pain, numbness, or tingling down the leg. Decompression may help reduce this pressure.
💧 Improves Nutrient Exchange
Unlike many tissues in the body, spinal discs have a very limited blood supply. The gentle stretching and relaxation cycles help encourage the movement of water, oxygen, and nutrients into the discs, supporting their health and recovery.
While spinal decompression can be beneficial for the right patient, it isn't a one-size-fits-all solution. A proper assessment is always important to determine the root cause of your pain.

Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis) is more than just shoulder pain or muscle tightness.
Many people believe it develops from overuse, but the real problem often occurs inside the shoulder joint capsule.
As inflammation builds, the capsule gradually thickens and stiffens, leading to shoulder stiffness, limited shoulder mobility, and difficulty performing simple daily activities like reaching overhead, dressing, or sleeping comfortably.
What makes frozen shoulder unique is its strong association with diabetes, thyroid disorders, and hormonal changes. These underlying conditions can influence the tissues surrounding the joint and increase the risk of developing adhesive capsulitis.
The good news? Early clinical assessment and the right physiotherapy approach can help manage pain, improve shoulder mobility, restore movement, and support shoulder rehabilitation.
Treatment is most effective when tailored to the stage of the condition rather than using the same exercises for everyone.
If your shoulder movement is gradually decreasing, don't ignore the warning signs. Understanding the cause is the first step toward recovery.

Still feeling stiff even after stretching every day?
The problem might not be your muscles it could be your joints.
Most people think tight hips or knees only need more stretching. But when a joint loses its ability to glide and move smoothly, stretching alone often isn't enough to restore normal movement.
In this video, we're using two physiotherapy techniques that target the joint itself:
✅ Hip Joint Mobilization
Gentle rotational movements help improve hip mobility, reduce capsule tightness, and restore smoother motion inside the joint.
✅ Lower Limb Traction & Joint Gliding
A controlled traction technique helps decompress the joint surfaces, allowing them to move more freely with less restriction.
Why does this matter?
When joints become stiff, your body starts compensating during walking, squatting, climbing stairs, and even simple daily activities. Over time, these movement compensations can contribute to discomfort, reduced mobility, and unnecessary strain on surrounding muscles.
💡 Remember:
Muscles need stretching.
Joints need mobilization.
The right combination can help you move better, feel lighter, and reduce that constant feeling of heaviness or stiffness.

I have been taking sessions from Dr Meghna Karia since almost 5 months now and it has been a great experience for me personally and has helped me grow in all areas of my life. She very skilled, experienced and gives you a great insight into your own life. She also makes you feel at ease which is great. Kudos !

featured_reviews.name: Aayushi Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: Ms Jenisha Shah is extremely patient and takes keen interest in knowing her clients. She is extremely skilled and professional and gives really good insights and inputs too. In a very short period of time, she’s helped me and taught me so much about life that has impacted me positively in many ways. Definitely one of the best at Mpower!

featured_reviews.name: Nishit Vora
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let me first start with stating that this has overall been a very enriching experience and progressively becoming a life altering experience.

I would like to call out Ms. Jenisha who showed immense patience with me and spent enough time to hear me out fully. She helped me break down each emotion, thought & word to help uncover deeper meanings to feelings which helped tackle concerns.

She’s exceptionally good at understanding human feeling and emotions and helped uplift spirits over time.

Kudos to her and the entire team for doing such a fantastic job

featured_reviews.name: Rohan Joseph George
featured_reviews.review_text: There is no zero star... Thats why I am giving one star. When I came here for a session they asked me whether I have suicide tendencies... Dude first of all I came here because I have mental health issues... Otherwise I wouldn't have come... When I said yes... They called my dad... Dude I am an adult... The psychologist who wrote my file after coming to know that sometimes I had suicidal tendencies in the past, she went and sat in another room chilling with the psychiatrist... She was not even present with me to explain the situation or to talk with me... Worst ever place... Don't ever go to this place. The name of the psychologist was Ms. Sanjana.. I don't remember her surname... Please don't go to her even when she starts a private practice or in some other place.

featured_reviews.name: RASHMI VAIDYA KULKARNI
featured_reviews.review_text: Ms Jenisha Shah has the knack to make her client feel at ease from the very first session itself. Her patience and ability to be a keen listener are certainly her most prominent skills. She has provided me with a very optimistic approach to life and continues to be an inspiration through every session. Surely one of the best that Mpower offers. Thanks Jenisha Ma'am.
